projects.name: Anvi Wadhwa
projects.description: CS undergraduate at VIT Chennai; ML, physical sciences, and reinforcement learning.
projects.displaytext:
Hi, I’m Anvi — CS undergraduate at VIT Chennai.

Welcome to my website. I don’t really have a neat, well-defined answer to who I am. The only thing I’m reasonably certain about is that I enjoy an unhealthy amount of larping. So, for now, let me just be Anvi Wadhwa, and welcome to Larpland.

Most of my curiosity currently lives in machine learning, particularly in areas involving physical and space sciences, probabilistic modeling, uncertainty quantification, and high-dimensional systems. Lately, I’ve been going deeper into reinforcement learning and the mathematics behind how agents learn, make decisions, and optimize behavior. Partly because it’s interesting. Partly because humans don’t seem particularly good at it either.

Outside computer science, I’m into philosophy, business, psychology, literature, and art. I love writing and chasing ideas that push boundaries. I appreciate anything that makes me question the obvious and look at the world sideways.

I don’t have a grand philosophy beyond staying curious. There are too many interesting things to learn, too many ideas to explore, and too many questions worth asking.

Congratulations. Now you’re about as me as I am.

categories.name: Projects
categories.description: Research and systems experiments currently in orbit.

projects.name: Predicting Failure in Offline Reinforcement Learning from Dataset Quality
projects.description: Investigating how fixed offline dataset quality and coverage drive failure modes in conservative offline RL (CQL, IQL) on D4RL. I study coverage reduction, quality degradation, and noise injection to predict failure before training; currently tracing a CQL collapse under degraded data quality.
projects.displaytext:
Investigating how fixed offline dataset quality and coverage drive failure modes in conservative offline RL (CQL, IQL) on D4RL. I study coverage reduction, quality degradation, and noise injection to predict failure before training; currently tracing a CQL collapse under degraded data quality.

Status: Ongoing

projects.name: Comparative Analysis of PPO and GRPO for Solving Wordle
projects.description: Trained PPO and GRPO agents across 2,309 official answer words. Compared win rate, guess efficiency, constraint reduction, policy entropy, and generalization. PPO converged to a stable, high-performing policy; GRPO later collapsed, exposing a gap between information-seeking and acting on information.
projects.displaytext:
Trained PPO and GRPO agents across 2,309 official answer words. Compared win rate, guess efficiency, constraint reduction, policy entropy, and generalization. PPO converged to a stable, high-performing policy; GRPO later collapsed, exposing a gap between information-seeking and acting on information.

Status: Research project

projects.name: Implementing Modern Large Language Models from First Principles
projects.description: Built a four-layer transformer from scratch on a personal-essay corpus. The first 10,000-step run overfit, with validation loss bottoming near step 1,100, so I capped training at 1,200 steps. The corpus is too small; scaling the data is next.
projects.displaytext:
Built a four-layer transformer from scratch on a personal-essay corpus. The first 10,000-step run overfit, with validation loss bottoming near step 1,100, so I capped training at 1,200 steps. The corpus is too small; scaling the data is next.

Status: In progress

projects.name: Reinforcement Learning for FTL Garbage Collection
projects.description: Built an FTL garbage-collection simulator in C and connected Python PPO agents through socket IPC. Benchmarked write amplification factor: PPO reached 15.1 versus 1.18 for greedy and 1.53 for random, motivating further training and tuning.
projects.displaytext:
Built an FTL garbage-collection simulator in C and connected Python PPO agents through socket IPC. Benchmarked write amplification factor: PPO reached 15.1 versus 1.18 for greedy and 1.53 for random, motivating further training and tuning.

Status: Research project

projects.name: Deep Sequence Learning for Stellar Photometry
projects.description: Designed an attention BiLSTM to predict stellar light curves from synthetic astronomical data. Evaluated sliding-window predictions across noise levels and window sizes using R², MAE, and MSE.
projects.displaytext:
Designed an attention BiLSTM to predict stellar light curves from synthetic astronomical data. Evaluated sliding-window predictions across noise levels and window sizes using R², MAE, and MSE.

Status: Research project

projects.description: A growing from-scratch RL library spanning Gymnasium CartPole, BipedalWalker, and Ant-v4, with training and evaluation pipelines for Q-Learning, DQN variants, PPO, and actor-critic methods.
projects.displaytext:

projects.name: Research Intern — IISER Bhopal
projects.description: Advised by Prof. Vivek Delukar · Grid Foundation Models for power systems
projects.displaytext:
Advised by Prof. Vivek Delukar

Grid Foundation Models for power systems

  • Researching self-supervised and graph-based power-grid representations.
  • Adapting and fine-tuning foundation models for grid analytics and forecasting.
  • Contributing literature and experimental analysis in AI for next-generation power systems.

projects.name: Computer Vision Research Intern — IIT (BHU) Varanasi
projects.description: Advised by Prof. Pankhuri Jain · Lower-Limb Pose Estimation for Physiotherapy Monitoring
projects.displaytext:
Advised by Prof. Pankhuri Jain

Lower-Limb Pose Estimation for Physiotherapy Monitoring

  • Built real-time tracking with MediaPipe and OpenCV for hip, knee, and ankle landmarks from webcam video.
  • Estimated joint angles and studied robustness across lighting, occlusion, and viewpoints.
  • Logged motion to CSV, visualized trajectories, and preprocessed exercise datasets.
